rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods <U+2013> field experiments established 2015 at NIHHS Wanju, Korea, with sprinkler, surface drip and subsurface drip treatments in three replications, water measured by flow meter. Q2: Results Exp. I and Table 2 <U+2013> water required to maintain the same matric potential was lower by 14% (surface drip) and 37% (subsurface drip) than sprinkler (188.1 vs 258.4 vs 299.7 Mg/10a); Results Exp. II and Table 5 <U+2013> subsurface drip at 30 cm used significantly less water than surface drip (138.4 vs 288.2 Mg/10a), 0 cm consuming 108% more. Q8: Conclusions <U+2013> results are for a single growing season; data from following years are needed to understand efficiency better. Q9: Table 5 <U+2013> irrigation water reported as mean <U+00B1> SE of three replications (288.2<U+00B1>33.8, 167.2<U+00B1>34.8, 138.4<U+00B1>25.3).
rows.notes: Single method (flow-meter volume under tensiometer-controlled scheduling); no measurement of soil evaporation or other intermediate variable explaining the saving. Note that in Table 2 (Exp. I, the source of the 37%/27% figures) all irrigation-water means carry the same letter, i.e. the differences were not statistically significant and no SE is printed for that column; only Exp. II (Table 5) shows a significant difference with SE. The conclusion that 30 cm depth is desirable is a recommendation, not stated as a requirement, so Q7 is no. One site, one crop (two rootstocks), plot scale. Text is inconsistent on year of water data (2018 stated in statistics section).

rows.evidence: Q1: Materials and methods <U+2013> own field experiment on 'Fuji'/M9 orchard with weed amount determined per 1 m3 in each treatment. Q2: Results Exp. I and Table 3 <U+2013> sprinkler had significantly higher weed amount (24.5 Mg/10a) followed by surface drip (23.7), while subsurface drip had significantly lower weed amount (20.7, letter b) than the other two methods. Q8: Conclusions <U+2013> results presented are for a single growing season; following years' data needed. Q9: Table 3 <U+2013> weed growth given as mean <U+00B1> SE of three replications (24.5<U+00B1>0.37, 23.7<U+00B1>0.32, 20.7<U+00B1>0.41).
rows.notes: Weed reduction measured by a single method (weed biomass sampling); the presumed mechanism (dry soil surface under buried emitters) is not measured. One site, one crop, plot scale, single season. No conditions stated as requirements for the weed effect; the authors also note weeds were controlled during the growing season, which limits interpretation of the weed data.

notes: Full text appears complete. Short primary field study (Korean J. Soil Sci. Fert. 2018) with two simultaneous experiments at one research station; limited statistical reporting (Table 2 lacks SE despite footnote and shows no significant differences in irrigation water for Exp. I).
